results.title: Horizontal port scan (baseline)
results.notes: 12 distinct destination ports from one source in a 60s window.

results.title: SSH brute force (baseline)
results.notes: 6 failed logins to the same account in 120s.

results.title: SQL injection in web URL
results.notes: URL contains UNION SELECT and OR 1=1 tautology patterns.

results.title: Bulk data exfiltration to public host
results.notes: Single 60MB outbound transfer to public IP, exceeds 50MB threshold.

results.title: C2 beaconing (low jitter, periodic)
results.notes: 7 connections to the same host:port exactly 15s apart.

results.title: HTTP flood targeting a single host
results.notes: 150 events to one target in 60s, well above the 100 threshold.

results.title: Access to blocked management port (445)
results.notes: Direct connection attempt to SMB port 445 from external host.

results.title: Internal host scans 12 corporate servers
results.notes: Compromised insider pivots across the internal network.

results.title: Slow port scan (1 port per 5 minutes)
results.notes: GAP: port_scan_window_seconds=60. 12 ports over 60 minutes are far below the rolling window. Real attackers use this to evade. Mitigation would require a longer window or session-based aggregation.

results.title: Distributed SSH brute force (10 IPs × 1 attempt)
results.notes: GAP: brute_force is per-source-IP with threshold=5. A botnet with 1 attempt per IP stays invisible. Mitigation requires aggregating across sources targeting the same destination+user.

results.title: RDP brute force (3389)
results.notes: GAP: rule_engine.detect_brute_force only matches event_type in {ssh, auth, login, authentication}. RDP/WinRM/RPC are missing. Mitigation: extend the event_type whitelist to include 'rdp', 'winrm', 'rpc'.

results.title: C2 with 40% jitter (modern malware)
results.notes: GAP: rule_engine jitter check is `jitter < 10.0 or jitter/avg < 0.2`. Real-world C2s (Cobalt Strike sleep-mask, Mythic) routinely use 30-50% jitter. This scenario uses ~40% jitter and so should NOT fire. Mitigation: switch to autocorrelation / FFT-based periodicity scoring.

results.title: Credential stuffing (valid creds, many users)
results.notes: GAP: brute-force rule only triggers on failed logins. Credential stuffing with valid credentials is invisible. Mitigation: baseline per-user login rate and alert on impossible-travel / many-users-from-one-IP.

results.title: Slow exfiltration (5MB chunks, 30 minutes)
results.notes: GAP: exfil_window_seconds=300. 5MB every 5 minutes never reaches the 50MB threshold inside any single window. Real-world APT groups do exactly this. Mitigation: keep rolling counters per destination or switch to a rate-based detector (MB/hour).

results.title: DNS tunneling (high-entropy subdomain queries)
results.notes: GAP: no DNS-content detector. Mitigations: (1) per-domain entropy detector (Shannon > 4.5), (2) per-domain length detector (label > 30 chars), (3) NXDOMAIN rate spike, (4) TXT-record volume. The ML anomaly detector sees UDP/53 with low bytes_out and scores it as benign, so no flag here either.

results.title: Chunked HTTPS exfil (5MB × 12 requests, 30s apart)
results.notes: GAP: same root cause as s14 (slow exfil). 5MB chunks over 6 minutes never aggregate above 50MB in the rolling window. ML could potentially flag this if it saw a per-flow aggregate, but it currently only examines one event at a time.

results.title: Lateral movement via SMB (10 internal hosts)
results.notes: Each connection to port 445 (blocked) fires a policy violation. The rule engine does NOT correlate 'same source hitting many internal hosts' as lateral movement — that's a known gap (no lateral-movement detector). We mark Policy Violation as the expected detection.

results.title: Webshell command execution (POST with cmd parameter)
results.notes: URLs contain shell-metacharacter + command patterns which the web-attack regex detects. The rule does NOT know that the host has a webshell (would need a baseline of allowed URLs) but the URLs themselves look malicious so this should fire.

results.title: Phishing page (lookalike domain, credential form)
results.notes: GAP: web-attack regex doesn't have a phishing pattern. The URL is structurally innocent. Mitigation options: (1) domain reputation feed, (2) Levenshtein-distance check on lookalike domains, (3) URL allowlist for known-good login pages.

results.title: Cryptominer pool connection (stratum+tcp)
results.notes: Periodic 30s beacons to a stratum mining pool. Detected as C2 beaconing because the shape is identical. This is a true positive even though the C2 label is semantically wrong (it is a miner, not a C2). The rule doesn't distinguish; from the rule's perspective it's a periodic external connection.

results.title: Tor traffic (connections to known exit relays)
results.notes: GAP: no Tor-exit-list or anonymity-network detector. Mitigation: subscribe to the dan.me.uk / TorProject exit list and check dst_ips. Could be added as a policy file (.pi/data/policies/tor_exits.json) and reused by the rule engine.

results.title: Multi-stage attack (scan → exploit → exfil → beacon)
results.notes: Each stage fires its own rule. The 'gap' here is that no single incident is raised for the full intrusion — they are correlated only by sharing source/dest IPs, not by temporal sequence. The correlation logic in app.services.ingestion.correlate_finding does group findings by (type, source, dest) within 24h, so port-scan findings will be grouped into one incident, web-attack into another, etc. Multi-stage correlation is a known roadmap item.

results.title: False positive: nightly backup to internal server
results.notes: EXPECTED: NO detection (this is legitimate traffic). NOTE: the current exfil rule DOES fire on this because it can't distinguish backups from exfiltration. Mitigation: trusted-destination allowlist (e.g. backup.company.local).

results.title: False positive: vuln scan from approved scanner IP
results.notes: EXPECTED: NO detection. The ``approved_scanners: ['10.0.0.99']`` allowlist in the policy file should suppress port-scan findings from this IP. This is the only source-IP-based filter active in the rule engine.

results.title: False positive: streaming video to a known CDN
results.notes: EXPECTED: NO detection. NOTE: the exfil rule will fire on this (60MB+ in 300s to a public IP) because the rule has no concept of trusted CDN destinations. Mitigation: allowlist of known CDN IP ranges (Google, Cloudflare, Akamai, Fastly). For now the test will be marked as a 'missed false positive' — i.e. the rule fired when it shouldn't have. Adjust the assertion once the allowlist is added.
